evidence: pull-service.lisp:438-448: (loop until (or (fnn-core ... 'fn-pull-session-done-p session) (fnn-pull-stoppingp runtime)) do ... (let ((incoming (receive))) ...)). receive is (fnn-recv fd +fnn-pull-read-seconds+ limit) with (defconstant +fnn-pull-read-seconds+ 60) at line 40. fnn-pull-worker (521-545) runs pull rounds, then fnn-catchup-tick, serially on one thread.
fix: Have ACL2 own a round budget (wall-clock or a minimum progress rate) and make its expiry a (:lost :timeout) event. Have ACL2 project the read, dial and send deadlines as the feed does for connect. Consider one worker per peer, or interleaving rounds by quantum, so one peer cannot starve the others.
notes: 2026-10-03 Groundwork explicitly authorized shared ACL2/native resumable transport capability; Runtime confirmed IO/owner API disjoint. S067 push-feed fairness and DNS availability remain separate frontiers unless actually consumed. No host wall cap or reused output/cold funding.

Implemented one-attempt TCP/TLS and retained pull/catch-up worker state; raw kernel/worker tests pass. PRF-1260 source/guard certification and actual saved-image SCN-1090 remain pending. No DNS deadline, push fairness, whole-round expiry or context-funding claim.
reviewer: pull-service.lisp:40 sets +fnn-pull-read-seconds+ to 60. receive (425-434) is a per-recv deadline. The loop (438-448) ends only on session-done or stopping, and the pull and catch-up session steps take no clock, so nothing bounds the whole round. The :dial arm uses :timeout 10 (351), not fn-owner-feed-connect-timeout as the push feed does (feed-service.lisp:157-158). fnn-pull-worker (521-545) runs pull and catch-up serially on one thread. The impact is limited to pull and catch-up liveness, and the peer must be configured, so the severity is low.
scenario: A configured (or compromised) pull peer answers NEWNEWS or XFNCATCHUP slowly, sending one byte every 59 s. Each fnn-recv returns data before its 60 s deadline, so the round never times out. Until the peer stops, no other peer is pulled and no catch-up round runs. The 60 s read and 10 s dial and send timeouts (line 351 uses :timeout 10, not ACL2's fn-owner-feed-connect-timeout the push feed uses) are host-chosen constants, not ACL2-owned bounds.
title: Pull and catch-up rounds have no overall time bound; one slow peer holds the only pull worker indefinitely
failure-message: healthy pull and catch-up must progress while slow pull retains partial state
